text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: GPU_MEMORY_PRESSURE_CLUSTER_EU-WEST-1 - threshold exceeded on pool 'dedicated-gpu-eu-1' (avg GPU mem usage 93%). Auto-throttle triggered.

pagerduty: Incident #INC-20260315-8347 - page sent to on-call (severity: P1) - route: eng-oncall -> primary -> Sophie (30s).

Sophie: ack'd via PagerDuty, i'm looking. seeing a spike in cuda alloc failures in the logs.

Kai: on it, pulling kubectl logs from runtime in eu-west-1 now. may be kv-cache evictions + fragmentation.

Linus: quick question - is this impacting hosted customers or only Dedicated? support-bot, any active customer tickets?

support-bot: Two active support threads flagged: CUST-1029 (dedicated) reporting high tail latency; CUST-1032 notes dropped requests during the window.

Sophie: customers on dedicated pools in eu-west show errors, hosted fallback already routing some traffic to eu-central. i'm going to push a temporary pool-shed config to reduce new allocations.

Eli: paste of the most recent error lines from runtime logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] ERROR runtime.cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation) at batcher.py:237
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] WARN runtime.kvcache: kv cache miss chain length 12 -> increased scatter allocs
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] ERROR runtime.kernel: cuCtxSynchronize failed: unspecified launch failure
```

Kai: that cuCtxSynchronize line suggests kernel timeouts following fragmentation. i'm going to cordon the worst nodes and drain so new inferences don't schedule there.

Sophie: agreed. i'm running the drain now on nodes: gpu-euw-12, gpu-euw-15, gpu-euw-16. command: `kubectl drain gpu-euw-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

Linus: will draining cause a short spike as pods reschedule? we should enable immediate fallback routing to eu-central for steady-state traffic. Sophie, can you flip routing?

Sophie: flipping routing policy to prefer eu-central for new requests. command: `infractl routing update --region-preference eu-central --reason "gpumem surge eu-west"`

pagerduty: Sophie acknowledged incident. Pager escalations at +3m to Kai if unresolved.

Kai: drain finished for gpu-euw-12/15/16. observed 18/42 pods recreated on eu-central, 8 fell back to cpu-quantized variant (slower but stable).

Eli: quick check: model-serving metrics show increased use of quantized-8bit for some heavy models -> cost will rise but availability maintained.

Sophie: checking node-level telemetry: nvml reports persistent reserved allocations that aren't freeing immediately. might be GPU driver bug combined with long-lived KV cache. i'm going to trigger a rolling restart of runtime service on the affected nodes after confirming low traffic.

Linus: note for postmortem - correlate with last runtime deploy at 02:30UTC. could be regression.

Kai: before restart, i'll try `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <id>` where supported; otherwise restart kubelet container to force driver teardown. doing gpu reset on gpu-euw-15 now.

Sophie: status update for customers: posting to status page draft -> "We are investigating GPU memory pressure in eu-west-1 causing increased latency for Dedicated customers. Traffic is being routed to alternate regions; mitigation in progress." anyone want to add specifics?

Eli: add that some requests are being served by a quantized fallback model and that we're seeing transient errors during kernel retries. keep wording non-technical.

support-bot: support queue annotated: CUST-1029 and CUST-1032 updated with mitigation and routing changes.

pagerduty: escalation to Kai sent (3m).

Kai: gpu reset returned `GPU reset not supported` on euw-15. proceeding with restarting runtime agent container.

Sophie: runtime agent restart complete on euw-15, nvml metrics show memory trending down, kv-cache eviction rate still elevated but stabilizing.

Linus: can we clear old KV cache shards safely? might help fragmentation. what's the command?

Eli: `runtime-cli kvcache trim --shard <shard-id> --policy aggressive` - use with caution, it will increase cold-start token cost for a bit. recommend after we confirm customer routing stable.

Kai: initiating trim on most-fragmented shard 7 during low traffic window in 2 minutes. will monitor for regressions.

Sophie: noticed a small spike in error 504s pinned to a canary model variant; pausing canary and promoting stable variant. `deployctl rollback --canary-id canary-20260314-9f2`

Kai: kv trim completed. memory fragmentation metrics improved ~12% within 30s. no new cudaAlloc errors in the last 60s on restarted nodes.

pagerduty: Incident still open. next escalation at +15m if not resolved.

Sophie: rolling restart on gpu-euw-12 and -16 scheduled and executed. all restarted nodes show healthy GPU memory freed. overall cluster mem usage dropping to 68% average.

Support-bot: customers notified: status page published. CUST-1029 acknowledged and confirmed reduced errors.

Linus: good. can we collect heap traces and driver logs for postmortem? i'll open an artifact collection run.

Sophie: started `artifacts collect --type nvml,driver,agent-logs --since 2026-03-15T09:00:00Z --nodes gpu-euw-*` job id A-8892.

Eli: recommend follow-up: add a throttle policy that preemptively reroutes when avg mem > 85% for >1m, and improve kv-cache eviction heuristics to avoid long chains.

Kai: agree. temporary mitigation successful. marking incident as "mitigated" but keeping it open for data collection and postmortem.

Sophie: closing loop: pagerduty incident acknowledged -> mitigated. i'll hand off next steps to Linus and postmortem owners. thanks all :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident #INC-20260315-8347 status: mitigated (acknowledged by Sophie) - resolving in 10m if no regressions.

Linus: will lead postmortem, timeline + mitigations to be drafted. leaving notes on root-cause hypotheses: driver memory leak under certain kv-cache fragmentation patterns; potential regression in runtime v2.1.3.

incident-bot: Automated follow-up: please attach artifacts (A-8892) and any `kubectl describe` outputs to the postmortem doc.

Sophie: done. handoff complete.

Eli: thanks everyone.

Kai: good job team.

support-bot: incident thread archived and tickets updated.
